question: How do you prevent catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuning a pretrained transformer on a small dataset?
reference_points: Lower learning rate and freeze most layers or use LoRA/adapters
Mix in some general data (replay) and use regularization
Early stopping and evaluate on both domain and general benchmarks
Fine-tune only as much as the task requires

question: What techniques optimize LLM inference speed in production?
reference_points: Quantization (FP16 to INT8/INT4) to shrink memory and compute
KV-cache management such as PagedAttention for throughput
Speculative decoding with a small draft model verified by the large one
Batching, distillation and efficient attention implementations

question: How do you handle LLM hallucinations and long-context limits, and when do you choose RAG over fine-tuning?
reference_points: Ground answers with retrieval (RAG), chunking and verified context
Prompting, self-consistency and guardrails reduce unsupported claims
RAG for fresh or private knowledge; fine-tuning for style, format and behavior
Check context limits, truncation and retrieval quality when long context fails

question: How do diffusion language models work, and how do they compare with autoregressive generation?
reference_points: Generate text by iteratively denoising or unmasking tokens, often many positions in parallel
Autoregressive models generate strictly left to right, one token at a time
Diffusion can use bidirectional context and may speed up generation
Autoregressive models remain the dominant, best-understood approach; compare on quality, speed and controllability

question: How do tensor shapes, dtypes and devices change from tokenizer output to model logits?
reference_points: Tokenizer gives input_ids and attention_mask of shape (batch, seq) as integer tensors, padded to equal length
Embedding layer produces (batch, seq, hidden) floating-point tensors
Final layer yields logits of shape (batch, seq, vocab)
Inputs and model must be on the same device; masks prevent attention to padding

question: How do you deploy an NLP model to production and scale it for high-throughput applications?
reference_points: Wrap the model in an API (FastAPI/Flask), containerize with Docker, serve behind a load balancer; use TorchServe or Triton for high traffic
Real-time inference needs small or optimized models and caching; batch inference can use larger models offline
Scale with replicas, async inference, model parallelism, and efficient models like DistilBERT
Reduce latency with quantization and distillation, and verify the accuracy impact

question: What does monitoring an NLP system in production look like?
reference_points: Operational metrics: latency, throughput, and error rates
Model signals: confidence score distributions, input length histograms, prediction distribution drift
Watch input vocabulary and topic shift, which can degrade performance before labeled evaluation catches it
Sample outputs for human review; define retraining triggers and alerts

question: How would you design a data pipeline for continuous text ingestion?
reference_points: Use a message queue or stream (Kafka, Pub/Sub) to buffer incoming text
Preprocess in parallel workers; make jobs idempotent and retryable
Store raw and processed versions separately so reprocessing is easy when logic changes
Handle deduplication, language detection, schema validation, and monitoring of lag

question: How do you decide between a classical ML model, a fine-tuned transformer, and LLM prompting for a text task?
reference_points: Classical models (logistic regression or SVM on TF-IDF): small data, tight latency or compute, strong interpretable baselines
Fine-tuned BERT-style models: enough labeled data and a stable task needing high accuracy at low per-request cost
LLM prompting: little labeled data, changing or open-ended tasks; costlier, slower, and less predictable
Benchmark all options on your own evaluation set for accuracy, latency, cost, and maintainability

question: What are the trade-offs between prompt tuning and full fine-tuning?
reference_points: Fine-tuning updates all weights: strongest performance but needs compute and a model copy per task
Prompt tuning learns soft prompt embeddings with the model frozen: very parameter-efficient and easy to serve many tasks
Prompt tuning tends to lag full fine-tuning at smaller model scales and converges closer at large scale
Related options: prefix tuning, adapters, and LoRA

question: What role does reinforcement learning play in NLP?
reference_points: Optimizes sequence-level objectives that are not differentiable, using reward signals
Uses: dialogue systems, summarization, machine translation, and text generation quality
RLHF aligns models to human preferences; alternatives include DPO and RLAIF
Challenges: reward design, reward hacking, training instability, and cost

question: How do you connect NLP model performance to business outcomes?
reference_points: Translate model metrics into business impact (e.g., F1 gain means fewer misrouted support tickets)
Define success metrics and cost of errors with stakeholders before building
Track online outcomes (resolution rate, conversion, handling time) alongside offline metrics
Use impact to prioritize improvements and decide when quality is good enough

question: How do you process documents longer than a transformer's token limit, and what are efficient transformer variants?
reference_points: BERT-style models cap input at about 512 tokens; naive truncation loses information
Strategies: chunk with overlap and aggregate predictions, hierarchical models, summarize first, or retrieve relevant passages
Efficient architectures use sparse or windowed attention (Longformer, BigBird) or low-rank/approximate attention (Linformer, Reformer)
Self-attention cost grows quadratically with length; choose by accuracy needs and compute budget
